title: Prospective Response Investigation by Multimodal Evaluation after Neoadjuvant Systemic Therapy prior to Radical Cystectomy (PRIME-RC)
summary: Patients with bladder cancer that has grown into the bladder muscle usually receive drug-based treatment before the planned surgical removal of the bladder. In some patients, this treatment causes the tumor to disappear completely. Whether this can already be reliably detected before surgery is currently not well understood. In this study, a bladder examination (cystoscopy) with a urine test and a small, low-risk tissue sample is therefore performed before the planned operation. The results are then compared with the actual findings in the tissue removed during surgery. In addition, several proteins are measured in the urine sample that is already being collected, to explore whether they provide further information about the response to treatment. Participation in the study does not change the planned treatment or the surgery itself.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Written informed consent prior to any study-related procedures
Histologically confirmed muscle-invasive urothelial carcinoma of the bladder or urothelial carcinoma with a muscle-invasive component; histological variants are permitted provided a clinical indication for radical cystectomy exists
Neoadjuvant systemic therapy administered as part of routine clinical care with planned radical cystectomy following completion or scheduled discontinuation of systemic therapy
Multidisciplinary tumor board decision or documented clinical indication for radical cystectomy
Availability of evaluable post-neoadjuvant cross-sectional imaging according to clinical standard prior to cystectomy
Ability to undergo cystoscopy and medical appropriateness of a cold cup biopsy
Exclusion criteria:
Lack of capacity to consent or absence of written informed consent
Inability to undergo cystoscopy or contraindication to cystoscopy/cold cup biopsy (e.g., active untreated urinary tract infection, clinically relevant uncompensated coagulation disorder, or other medically relevant safety concerns)
Absence of evaluable post-neoadjuvant cross-sectional imaging
Primary metastatic stage cM1 at the time of planned radical cystectomy, unless a curative-intent cystectomy is still planned
Planned alternative definitive therapy instead of radical cystectomy (e.g., primary trimodal therapy or primary partial cystectomy)
Withdrawal of consent
